jp: 毎週[まいしゅう]、母[はは]に手紙[てがみ]を{出[だ]します|cl-dasu}。
en: Every week I mail a letter to my mother.
why: Mailing a letter is 手紙を出す; the letter leaves your hands into the postal system.

jp: 郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]で手紙[てがみ]を{出[だ]しました|cl-dasu}。
en: I mailed a letter at the post office.
why: 手紙を出す is the set phrase for posting a letter.

jp: 昨日[きのう]書[か]いた手紙[てがみ]を、今[いま]からポストに{出[だ]しに行[い]きます|cl-dasu}。
en: I'm going to drop the letter I wrote yesterday into the mailbox now.
why: Putting a letter in the mailbox is 手紙を出す; the other verbs do not pair with 手紙 here.

jp: 友達[ともだち]に手紙[てがみ]を{出[だ]したい|cl-dasu}です。
en: I want to send a letter to a friend.
why: 手紙を出す is the verb for sending a letter by post; かける and つける do not take 手紙.

jp: 手紙[てがみ]を{出[だ]す|cl-dasu}ときは、切手[きって]を貼[は]ってください。
en: When you mail a letter, please put a stamp on it.
why: The verb that goes with 手紙 for posting it is 出す.

jp: 祖父[そふ]は毎年[まいとし]、お礼[れい]の手紙[てがみ]を{出[だ]しています|cl-dasu}。
en: My grandfather sends a thank-you letter every year.
why: Sending a letter by post is 手紙を出す, here as a repeated habit with ている.

jp: この手紙[てがみ]を今日[きょう]中[じゅう]に{出[だ]してください|cl-dasu}。
en: Please mail this letter today.
why: Asking someone to post a letter uses 出す; かける and つける do not fit 手紙.

jp: 明日[あした]までに宿題[しゅくだい]を{出[だ]してください|cl-dasu}。
en: Please hand in your homework by tomorrow.
why: Handing in homework is 宿題を出す.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は毎日[まいにち]たくさん宿題[しゅくだい]を{出[だ]します|cl-dasu}。
en: The teacher gives a lot of homework every day.
why: Teachers assign homework with 宿題を出す.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]を{出[だ]さなかった|cl-dasu}ので、先生[せんせい]に怒[おこ]られました。
en: I didn't hand in my homework, so the teacher got angry with me.
why: Submitting homework is 宿題を出す; the negative past states that it was not handed in.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]が多[おお]くて、まだ{出[だ]していません|cl-dasu}。
en: I had so much homework that I still haven't handed it in.
why: 宿題を出す means to hand in homework; ていません reports that it has not happened yet.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]みの宿題[しゅくだい]を、やっと{出[だ]しました|cl-dasu}。
en: I finally handed in my summer vacation homework.
why: 宿題を出す is the verb for handing in homework.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]を{出[だ]す|cl-dasu}のを忘[わす]れて、先生[せんせい]にあやまりました。
en: I forgot to hand in my homework and apologized to the teacher.
why: 宿題を出す is the fixed phrase for handing in homework.

jp: 先生[せんせい]、来週[らいしゅう]の宿題[しゅくだい]はもう{出[だ]しましたか|cl-dasu}。
en: Teacher, have you already assigned next week's homework?
why: A teacher assigning homework is 宿題を出す.

jp: 大[おお]きい声[こえ]を{出[だ]して|cl-dasu}、本[ほん]を読[よ]んでください。
en: Please read the book aloud in a loud voice.
why: Producing a loud voice is 声を出す; 声をかける would mean calling out to someone.

jp: 赤[あか]ちゃんが寝[ね]ているので、声[こえ]を{出[だ]さないで|cl-dasu}ください。
en: The baby is sleeping, so please don't make any noise.
why: Making a sound with your voice is 声を出す; the negative request asks for silence.

jp: 歌[うた]うときは、お腹[なか]から声[こえ]を{出[だ]す|cl-dasu}といいですよ。
en: When you sing, it is good to produce your voice from the belly.
why: 声を出す means to produce your voice; none of the other verbs does that.

jp: 彼[かれ]は怒[おこ]っても、大[おお]きな声[こえ]を{出[だ]しません|cl-dasu}。
en: Even when he is angry, he never raises his voice.
why: 声を出す is used for speaking or shouting aloud, here with 大きな.

jp: 遠[とお]くの友達[ともだち]に聞[き]こえるように、大[おお]きな声[こえ]を{出[だ]しました|cl-dasu}。
en: I shouted loudly so that my friend far away could hear.
why: Speaking loudly is 声を出す; the other verbs cannot take 声 in this meaning.

jp: もっと声[こえ]を{出[だ]して|cl-dasu}、挨拶[あいさつ]しましょう。
en: Let's say hello in a louder voice.
why: 声を出す means to use your voice audibly; the English asks for more volume.

jp: 犬[いぬ]が怖[こわ]くて、思[おも]わず声[こえ]を{出[だ]してしまいました|cl-dasu}。
en: The dog scared me, and I cried out without meaning to.
d: 取[と]ってしまいました
送[おく]ってしまいました
why: A sound escaping from you is 声を出す; the other verbs do not fit 声.

jp: 試験[しけん]に落[お]ちても、元気[げんき]を{出[だ]してください|cl-dasu}。
en: Even if you fail the exam, please cheer up.
why: Cheering up is 元気を出す, literally 'bring out your spirit'.

jp: 落[お]ち込[こ]んでいる友達[ともだち]に「元気[げんき]を{出[だ]して|cl-dasu}」と言[い]いました。
en: I said "Cheer up" to my friend who was feeling down.
why: The encouragement phrase is 元気を出して, 'cheer up'.

jp: 負[ま]けても元気[げんき]を{出[だ]せば|cl-dasu}、また勝[か]てますよ。
en: Even if you lose, if you keep your spirits up you can win again.
why: 元気を出す means to cheer up or keep your spirits up; the other verbs do not form this idiom.

jp: 友達[ともだち]が失恋[しつれん]したので、早[はや]く元気[げんき]を{出[だ]して|cl-dasu}ほしいです。
en: My friend just went through a breakup, so I want them to cheer up soon.
why: 元気を出す is the idiom for cheering up; てほしい says you want the friend to do it.

jp: 母[はは]は私[わたし]が泣[な]いているとき、いつも「元気[げんき]を{出[だ]しなさい|cl-dasu}」と言[い]います。
en: When I'm crying, my mother always says, "Cheer up."
why: 元気を出す is the standard way to tell someone to cheer up.

jp: そんなに暗[くら]い顔[かお]をしないで、元気[げんき]を{出[だ]しましょう|cl-dasu}。
en: Don't look so gloomy; let's cheer up.
why: 元気を出す is the idiom for cheering up.

jp: 長[なが]い会議[かいぎ]のあとで、やっと結論[けつろん]を{出[だ]しました|cl-dasu}。
en: After the long meeting, we finally reached a conclusion.
why: Reaching a conclusion is 結論を出す.

jp: 結論[けつろん]を{出[だ]す|cl-dasu}前[まえ]に、もう少[すこ]し調[しら]べましょう。
en: Before we reach a conclusion, let's investigate a little more.
why: 結論を出す is the fixed phrase for drawing or reaching a conclusion.

jp: この問題[もんだい]については、まだ結論[けつろん]を{出[だ]していません|cl-dasu}。
en: We haven't reached a conclusion on this problem yet.
why: 結論を出す means to come to a conclusion; ていません says it has not happened yet.

jp: 急[いそ]いで結論[けつろん]を{出[だ]さない|cl-dasu}ほうがいいと思[おも]います。
en: I think it's better not to rush to a conclusion.
why: 結論を出す is the verb for reaching a conclusion; ないほうがいい gives the advice not to.

jp: 話[はなし]が長[なが]くなるので、早[はや]く結論[けつろん]を{出[だ]してください|cl-dasu}。
en: The discussion is getting long, so please reach a conclusion quickly.
why: Asking someone to wrap up with a conclusion is 結論を出す.

jp: 委員会[いいんかい]は来月[らいげつ]までに結論[けつろん]を{出[だ]す|cl-dasu}予定[よてい]です。
en: The committee plans to reach a conclusion by next month.
why: 結論を出す is the set phrase; the other verbs do not combine with 結論.

jp: 月曜日[げつようび]の朝[あさ]、燃[も]えるごみを{出[だ]します|cl-dasu}。
en: On Monday morning I put out the burnable trash.
why: Putting trash out for collection is ごみを出す.

jp: ごみを{出[だ]す|cl-dasu}日[ひ]を間違[まちが]えて、近所[きんじょ]の人[ひと]に注意[ちゅうい]されました。
en: I got the day for putting out the trash wrong, and a neighbor warned me.
why: ごみを出す is the phrase for putting trash out on collection day.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]に行[い]く前[まえ]に、ごみを{出[だ]して|cl-dasu}くれる？
en: Could you take out the trash before you go to work?
why: ごみを出す means to take the trash out to the collection point.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は、ごみを{出[だ]し|cl-dasu}忘[わす]れました。
en: Yesterday I forgot to put out the trash.
why: ごみを出す, here in its stem form before 忘れる, means to put out the trash.

jp: ここにごみを{出[だ]して|cl-dasu}はいけません。
en: You must not put trash out here.
why: ごみを出す is the phrase for putting trash out; てはいけません forbids it.

jp: ごみを{出[だ]した|cl-dasu}あとで、手[て]を洗[あら]いました。
en: After putting out the trash, I washed my hands.
why: ごみを出す means to take trash out for collection.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]は収集[しゅうしゅう]がないので、ごみを{出[だ]さないで|cl-dasu}ください。
en: There is no collection on Sundays, so please don't put out trash.
why: ごみを出す is putting trash out; the negative request says not to.

jp: 友達[ともだち]の結婚祝[けっこんいわ]いに、みんなで少[すこ]しずつお金[かね]を{出[だ]しました|cl-dasu}。
en: For our friend's wedding gift, everyone chipped in a little money.
why: Contributing money toward something is お金を出す.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]のお金[かね]は、全部[ぜんぶ]私[わたし]が{出[だ]します|cl-dasu}。
en: I'll pay all the money for the trip myself.
why: Paying or putting up money is お金を出す; 借ります would mean borrowing it.

jp: 母[はは]が学費[がくひ]のお金[かね]を{出[だ]して|cl-dasu}くれました。
en: My mother paid my tuition for me.
why: お金を出す means to put up or pay money; 取って would mean she took it.

jp: 誰[だれ]がお金[かね]を{出[だ]す|cl-dasu}か、まだ決[き]まっていません。
en: It hasn't been decided yet who will pay the money.
why: Who puts up the money is お金を出す.

jp: もう少[すこ]しお金[かね]を{出[だ]せば|cl-dasu}、もっといいカメラが買[か]えますよ。
en: If you pay a little more money, you can buy a better camera.
why: Handing over or paying money is お金を出す; 取れば would mean receiving it.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]はこのプロジェクトにお金[かね]を{出[だ]さない|cl-dasu}そうです。
en: I hear the company will not put up money for this project.
why: Funding something is お金を出す; the negative says the company will not pay.

jp: いくらお金[かね]を{出[だ]しても|cl-dasu}、時間[じかん]は買[か]えません。
en: No matter how much money you pay, you can't buy time.
why: お金を出す means to pay out money; ても gives 'no matter how much'.
